name: Never Too Much
description: Never Too Much is the debut solo album by Luther Vandross, released in 1981 on Epic Records. After a decade as an elite background vocalist and a stint fronting the group Change, Vandross arrived with complete command of his instrument and his arrangements. The title track, bright and bouncing, became his signature song; “Don’t You Know That?” and his reading of “A House Is Not a Home” displayed the ballad control that would define the R&B love song for a decade. The album opened an unbroken run of eleven consecutive platinum albums, a streak the standard biographies record as a first for an R&B artist of his era, and it established the template — immaculate production, conversational phrasing, choruses built to be lived in — that Vandross refined for the rest of his career. Never Too Much is the sound of a singer who had spent ten years learning exactly where the microphone was, stepping up to it at last on his own name.

name: Nikki Giovanni
description: Nikki Giovanni (born Yolanda Cornelia Giovanni, June 7, 1943, Knoxville, Tennessee; died December 9, 2024, Virginia) was a poet, writer, and educator who emerged as a leading voice of the Black Arts Movement. Educated at Fisk University, where she graduated in 1967, she published her first volumes, Black Feeling, Black Talk (1968) and Black Judgment (1969), followed by Re: Creation (1970), and went on to write dozens of poetry collections, essays, and eleven illustrated children's books. Her honors included seven NAACP Image Awards for Literature, the Langston Hughes Award, and the Frost Medal for lifetime achievement in poetry. Giovanni taught at Rutgers from 1969 and at Virginia Tech from 1987 to 2022, where she was named University Distinguished Professor and remained on the faculty until her death. Her work moved between public witness — race, history, and collective grief — and an intimate register of family, place, and joy.

name: Ne-Yo
description: Ne-Yo, born Shaffer Chimere Smith on 18 October in Camden, Arkansas, and raised in Las Vegas, Nevada, is an American singer and one of the defining R&B songwriters of his generation. He broke through as a writer, co-writing Mario's "Let Me Love You" (2004), which led to a Def Jam deal; he went on to write Beyoncé's "Irreplaceable" and Rihanna's "Take a Bow." His debut album In My Own Words (2006) reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 behind the Hot 100 No. 1 "So Sick," followed by Because of You (2007) and Year of the Gentleman (2008). He has won three Grammy Awards, including Best Contemporary R&B Album for Because of You and two awards for "Miss Independent." His birth year is contested across sources — 1979 in the current reference record, 1982 and 1983 in others — and is carried here as unresolved rather than blended.

name: Nicki Minaj
description: Nicki Minaj (born Onika Tanya Maraj on December 8, 1982, in Saint James, Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago) is a Trinidadian rapper, singer and songwriter raised in Queens, New York, and widely dubbed the “Queen of Rap.” After three mixtapes between 2007 and 2009, she signed with Young Money Entertainment; her debut album, Pink Friday (2010), topped the Billboard 200 and produced the Diamond-certified single “Super Bass.” Pink Friday: Roman Reloaded (2012), The Pinkprint (2014) and Queen (2018) consolidated her position, and her guest verse on Kanye West's “Monster” is routinely cited among the greatest rap verses of its era. Pink Friday 2 (2023) made her the first female rapper with three US number-one albums, and “Super Freaky Girl” became her first solo Hot 100 number one. She has been nominated for twelve Grammy Awards.

name: Naomi
aliases: Trinity Fatu; Trinity McCray; Trinity; Naomi Knight
description: Trinity Fatu, born Trinity McCray on 30 November 1987 in Sanford, Florida, is an American professional wrestler signed to WWE, where she performs as Naomi. A former Orlando Magic dancer, she entered WWE's developmental system in 2009, became the inaugural FCW Divas Champion, and reached the main roster as one half of the Funkadactyls before remaking herself as a singles star known for her athleticism and 'Glow' presentation. She is a three-time women's world champion in WWE and a two-time Women's Tag Team Champion. After walking out of WWE in 2022 she rebuilt her name in TNA as Trinity, winning the Knockouts World Championship, then returned to WWE in 2024. In 2025 she won the women's Money in the Bank ladder match and cashed in at Evolution to win the Women's World Championship again. She relinquished that title in August 2025 after announcing her pregnancy, welcomed her first child in 2026, and was reported in late September 2026 to be the subject of WWE return preparations.
